source.title: Mean Shift Rejection: Training Deep Neural Networks Without Minibatch Statistics or Normalization
source.authors: B. Ruff; Taylor Beck; Joscha Bach

record.tranche_reason: Reports CIFAR-10 ResNet110 training results under several recipes, including a comparison with batch normalization, but does not reproduce the claim’s full set of benchmarks or interventions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports training-accuracy curves, but gives no textual final training-error values. Table 1 reports test accuracy, which is not a measure of the claim’s training-error outcome. The initialization and hyperparameter details used only to set up experiments are not separate results.
record.test_reason: The study reports its own ResNet110 training-accuracy curves on CIFAR-10 under SGD, bearing on V1. The supplied text omits the plotted values, so whether training error approaches zero cannot be determined.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate: the authors report stable, high-learning-rate ResNet110 training without normalization or minibatch statistics, and higher, more consistent test accuracy than their batch-normalized baseline. This conclusion concerns test accuracy and stability, not demonstrated near-zero training error. Their broader architectural applicability remains conjectural.
record.recipe_differences: Uses ResNet110 on CIFAR-10 with channel-wise zero-mean initialization and gradient modification; the supplied claim’s broader recipe includes CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 and corrupted or random labels.
record.method_sensitivity: The text reports that zmg factor affects training rate and final accuracy for ResNets; zmg=1 at learning rate 0.4 diverges, and noise injection changes test accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: CZMIG with noise achieves 94.03±0.14% test accuracy versus 93.70±0.55% for the batch-normalized baseline.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An alternative normalization-free training recipe can improve CIFAR-10 test accuracy over this batch-normalized ResNet110 baseline.

fits_no_version.finding: CZMI is reported stable at learning rates 0.1, 0.2, and 0.4; exact zero-mean gradient enforcement diverges at the higher rate.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learning-rate tolerance in this ResNet110 recipe depends on initialization and the strength of the gradient constraint; this does not establish recovery above a measured stability threshold.

record.problems: Training-error outcomes are presented only as plots and are not numerically described in the text; the experiments use one architecture and dataset.
record.rows_left_out: No additional training-accuracy figure conditions extracted beyond the representative CZMI, CZMIG, noise-injected CZMIG, and batch-normalization runs; the remaining plotted variants are not separately described with textual training-error outcomes.

untested.parts: CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, smaller-model comparisons, early stopping, and Adam. The supplied text does not resolve near-zero training error even for the tested CIFAR-10 conditions.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious local minima, and student-width interventions.
Depth comparisons, plain versus residual networks, very deep plain tanh networks, and Fixup.
Activation-matched initialization comparisons in plain networks, signal or gradient propagation across depth, and orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization.
Initial linearized stability limits, curvature trajectories, catapult recovery, and full-batch edge-of-stability behavior.

The effect of adding batch normalization to an otherwise matched recipe, comparative convergence speed, learning-rate tolerance under that intervention, and Fixup. The alternative recipe changes initialization, updates, parameterization, regularization, and noise.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source listed for any version. No verdict is justified from the available V1 rows because the training-accuracy plots are not readable in the supplied text. Table 1 contains test accuracy and cannot substitute for training accuracy. Additional plotted variants are already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, smaller models, early stopping, and Adam; the text does not state numerical final training error.

rows.subject: ResNet110
rows.operation_detail: CIFAR-10 training with channel-wise zero-mean initialization only (CZMI), without gradient adaptation
rows.note: Training accuracy is plotted, but the text gives no final training-accuracy or training-error value.
rows.check: The supplied Figure 1 caption and discussion do not give final training accuracy. CZMI here also uses reparameterization and unity magnitude anchoring; it is not an isolated initialization intervention.

rows.subject: ResNet110
rows.operation_detail: CIFAR-10 training with channel-wise zero-mean initialization plus channel-wise zero-mean gradient updates (CZMIG)
rows.note: The text says training accuracy increases monotonically after annealing steps; it does not state a final training-error value.
rows.check: Monotonic accuracy increases after annealing do not establish near-zero training error. The recipe also includes reparameterization and unity magnitude anchoring.

rows.subject: ResNet110
rows.operation_detail: CIFAR-10 training with CZMIG and noise injection
rows.note: Training-accuracy curves are shown, but no numerical final training-error result is stated.
rows.check: No readable final training-accuracy value is supplied. Figures 3–5 include multiple conditions; this row should identify specifically the zmg=0.85, learning-rate=0.4, noise-amplitude=0.1 condition.

rows.subject: ResNet110
